rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: DRIFT RE-CHECK against current §1 wording (rule.js slides 1). Chunk 5 'the window' (raw line 58) resolves via chunk-0 title reuse ('map the window', raw line 1) and chunk 4's own heading ('how full the window is', raw line 45) — same carve-out class as the compendium's own 'the map' / the-whole-map.md example. 'Your repo' / 'it' throughout resolve via the session-artifact carve-out (student's own repo, prework-chosen; see maintainer 'Plug points'). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: DRIFT RE-CHECK against current §15 wording (rule.js slides 15, generalized 2026-08-19). Four headings (raw lines 21, 31, 40, 45) are plain imperatives. The closer 'The slice Claude didn't load' (raw line 55) is a bare noun phrase with no independent main verb — grammatically a topic-naming label (parallel to the compendium's own worked non-violation 'The numbers'), not a subject+predicate assertion like the compendium's two counted exercise declaratives ('Anything can be reverse-engineered', 'There is always a next plausible answer'). It therefore reads under the catalogue-entry-naming-subject carve-out, not the claim requirement; consistent with the compendium's own house-norm measurement (2/108 exercise headings are true declaratives). The generalizing claim itself lives in the chunk's body bullets (raw lines 57-58), which is where §15's two counted precedents also place their generalisation — the header there just happens to also be phrased as the assertion, this one is not, and nothing in the rule requires it to be.
